base_record_snapshot.lesson: Reading the authoritative manifest is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT — a RETIRED predicate applied to the correct source still lies, and it lies quietly because both numbers look plausible. Lived at tic 680: the conformation artifact carries two counters over the same substrate, and they disagree by 2. counts.active_signals = 57, computed with the shared is_active_ray predicate (structurally live, or carried/dimmed with heat above floor). governance_query_enrichment.manifold_summary.active = 55, computed by filtering on the RAW STATUS ENUM — the predicate the federation has explicitly RETIRED. The delta is fully accounted with zero residue: exactly the 2 rays whose raw status is 'acknowledged' (sig_2026-04-05_vpl_composite_rollback_gap, sig_economy_economy_fetch_failed_84fb94e38d7a), both structurally live. This refines the existing authoritative-set-readers invariant, which was written against readers that aggregate RAW EMISSIONS instead of the curated manifest. Here BOTH readers read the curated manifest correctly and still disagree — the divergence is in the PREDICATE, one layer below sourcing. So predicate retirement carries the same closed-consumer-set obligation that a structural transform carries: retiring a predicate silently obligates an update on every reader that still applies it, and a reader inside the SAME artifact as the correct one is the easiest to miss precisely because the artifact looks internally authoritative. Disagreement-as-evidence held: the 2-count gap was the visible symptom of a stale predicate, not a counting bug to arbitrate.
